newsitem.title: USA: Suspect arrested in New York rail hostage-taking.
newsitem.headline: Suspect arrested in New York rail hostage-taking.

text.p: Hundreds of people were held hostage on a suburban New York train commandeered Monday by a suspect who was later arrested, police said.
It was not immediately clear what weapon the suspect used or what his motive was, a police spokesman said. No injuries were reported.

The suspect forced the Long Island Rail Road train, carrying 450 people, to stop at the Wayandanch, N.Y., station, about 40 miles east of New York City, police said. He took control of the train at the station for about 30 minutes until he was taken into police custody, Suffolk County Police Officer Randy Jarret said.

The train had been scheduled to arrive at New York City's Penn Station at 11:28 a.m., a Long Island Rail Road spokesman said. Police also were investigating whether the suspect had any connection to a bank robbery Monday morning in nearby Brentwood, N.Y., Jarret said.
